_meta.title: Events calendar for the simulation: Xerxes yr 19 = 1 Nisannu (17 Apr 467 BCE) to 29 Addaru (5 Apr 466 BCE)
_meta.doc: research/EVENTS.md (ids E-xx and CE-xx match); populations and ration templates in src/data/population.json
_meta.tiers: A attested / B inferred (includes all search-extract values) / C reconstructed. Most rhythms are C: the dated evidence is Darius-era (PF, 509-493) and only 67 PF texts were read in full (CDLI-PF).
_meta.court_state: default court_absent (D-003). Events with 'setting': 'court_resident' run only when the out-of-world setting 'Court calendar = seasonal pattern' is on (resident months 1-4).
_meta.months_field: Babylonian month numbers of year 19 (1 = Nisanu ... 12 = Addaru), or "all"

rule_types.monthly: once per month per unit (group, household ...) on a day drawn from day_range (day 1 = first day of the Babylonian month)
rule_types.daily: every day in the listed months, between hours (local solar time) when given
rule_types.rate: Poisson arrivals with the given mean per 'per' (day | week | month | year), clipped to range
rule_types.per_1000_per_year: per-capita annual rate applied to the simulated population of the zone(s)
rule_types.trigger: fires when the named event or state change occurs
rule_types.state: a continuous state keyed by month, not a discrete event
rule_types.never: documented but not scheduled (kept so that the gap is visible)
rule_types.mass_balance: deliveries sized so the stores meet the modelled outlays over the year (E-06b; DECISIONS D-021, Q-056)

_meta.effects_grammar: pseudo-code for the simulation engineer, not executable: store.X -= qty; agent.need += x; group.flag = v; spawn(template); schedule(E-xx)

months.gloss: (month) of the worship of the fire

months_src.tier: A (Babylonian dates); B (Persian names, SX); glosses are etymologies, not evidence of practice

events.name: monthly grain ration issue to a work group (L texts)
events.place_kind: storehouse (town); Terrace depot for Terrace gangs

goods.qty: sum of population.json ration_scale over the group (Liduma group: 261.5 BAR)

events.note: scale and roles B/A; the day of issue is not recorded (C; Q-034)

events.name: wine or beer ration for workers
events.note: the act is attested (PF 50, 'for rations of workers', A Darius-era); how often, and for which groups, is unknown (Q-045)

events.name: special ration (M texts): an extra day's ration
events.note: 'most commonly an extra day's ration per month' (SX); the probability is C

events.name: mother's ration after a birth (N texts)
preconditions: mother is in a state ration group
events.note: single payment, boy twice girl: B. The amounts are C (NS; conflicting SX '2 vs 1 quarts'; Q-030)

events.name: silver paid at the Treasury in lieu of part or all of a group's sheep, wine or grain rations

goods.qty: chief of 100: 32.5; ordinary worker: 1-1.5 per month in lieu (C placeholder)

preconditions: a letter or memorandum from an ordering official for a completed work period
effects: the group's in-kind ration for that period is reduced by the part paid in silver
events.note: practice B; rhythm C: 753 PT tablets over 492-458, with the most dated texts in yrs 19-20 -> 110-150 documents a year if 30-40 % fall in those years (Q-033 for rates)

events.name: grain delivery to the royal stores at Persepolis

goods.unit: BAR per consignment (median of the read texts ~ 100-400)

events.note: quantities A (PF 2-8, 26, 30-33); seasonality C: only PF 6 (months 4-6) and PF 7 (month 8) are dated to the month

events.name: grain (with a little tarmu) brought in to the ration storehouse from the harvest, sized to the outlays

rule.sized_to: 12 months of the ration groups' demand + the work-camp bread + transferred groups (E-23), times the year's harvest factor (0.9-1.1), less the expected E-06 deliveries

events.note: balance row (DECISIONS D-021): the read E-06 consignments (6-3000 BAR, median 100-400) at the E-06 rate (~57 a year, i.e. roughly 6,000-23,000 BAR) cannot feed the ~2,700 people in ration groups (~7,400 BAR a month, ~89,000 a year), so the ration store is also filled in the E-06 seasonal shape, sized to the outlays. The PF record receipts and outlays of the same suppliers, not the balance (Q-056). Shown in the world as ordinary E-06 deliveries.

events.name: grain to the mill (nupištaš), flour back to the stores
events.note: the flow is A (PF 28-29 'taken to the nupištaš (i.e. the mill?)'; flour consignments PF 30-33, 54); the rhythm and the conversion loss are C

events.name: beer brewed from tarmu
events.note: PF 40: 700 BAR tarmu ... 'He made beer' (A, Darius-era); rhythm C

events.name: wine delivery
events.note: quantities A (PF 41-52); the post-vintage peak is C

events.name: figs and fruit to the royal stores
events.note: PF 53 (A); the season is C

events.name: sesame moved to stores
events.note: PF 56 (A); the season is C

events.name: stockyard slaughter; hides delivered to the treasury
events.note: PF 58-60 (FT; Darius-era, Hiran and Shiraz treasuries; PF 60 in month 1); the rate is C

events.name: tax animals and 'the sheep of the king' driven to Susa
events.place_kind: road west out of the plain
events.note: PF 57: 4 tax animals to Susa (A); ~700 shepherds with the king's sheep (SX, B); the month is C

events.name: flour drawn 'in the treasury' for the kurakaraš
events.note: PF 403-406 (FT; Darius-era, other treasuries); kurakaraš is untranslated. Carried to Persepolis in 467: C

events.name: sealed receipts filed; stock counted
events.note: tablets sealed by supplier and recipient go back as the record (B); the rhythm is C

events.name: express courier (pirradaziš) arrives or leaves
events.place_kind: road station (town edge); sealed letters carried up to the Treasury
preconditions: none: 'stopped neither by snow nor rain nor heat nor darkness' (HDT 8.98)
effects: a fresh horse is issued; the tired horse is stabled
schedule(E-81) if the letter is for the Treasury
events.note: institution B (Greek claims plus PF); the rate is C

events.name: a party with a sealed authorisation (halmi) arrives and draws travel rations

participants.role: party leader named on the halmi

events.place_kind: road station / storehouse; lodging in the town
preconditions: the party holds a halmi from the king or a satrap-level official
events.note: practice and scale B; the rate and party sizes are C (Q-041)

events.name: a large work group arrives (reassigned kurtaš)

goods.unit: qa per head per day in transit

effects: the monthly ration demand rises from the next month
events.note: practice B (1,633 Lycian marataš); the months and rate are C

events.name: gift-bearing delegation
events.note: none while the king is absent (D-003). Whether the Apadana reliefs show a real annual procession is debated (brief section 2); even with the court resident, no delegation is scheduled unless evidence is found

events.name: the court arrives
events.place_kind: road from Susa -> Terrace, palaces, town
effects: populations switch to court_resident over 1-3 days

events.name: the court leaves
effects: populations return to court_absent over 7-14 days (CE-18)

events.name: journeys to the king at the New Year

participants.role: officials and taxpayers with their parties

events.note: a Darius-era pattern (B, abstract only)

events.name: lan: the regular (daily) sacrifice, drawn as an allocation by a magus or priest

goods.unit: qa per month for lan (C: PF 1955's 90-qa share, if the text covers a year)

effects: the priest's keep is covered (lan as basic income)
events.performance: minimal: the allocation is received and carried to the offering place. No invented liturgy. If a sacrifice is ever shown: no altar, no fire, no music; the magus chants (HDT 1.132, claim)
events.note: Darius-era PF; continuity in 467 and the place are C (Q-035)

events.name: offering to a named mountain and a named river
events.note: PF 1955 and the journals of the magi Kammargina and Upiš (SX); rate C

events.name: offering for gods: Mišebaka ('All Gods'), Auramazdā, Humban, Napiriša, Adad, Šimut

goods.item: barley or wine; sheep for larger offerings

events.note: gods and relative weight from SX (Humban's grain more than 3x Auramazdā's); rates C

events.name: šip: large sacrificial feast connected with the crown
events.place_kind: attested at Pasargadae and Appištapdan, not at Persepolis
preconditions: a presiding high official is present (none attested in 467)
events.note: Darius-era (Parnakka, Ziššawiš; NN 2259); not scheduled by default

events.name: the king's birthday feast (tukta)
effects: the king anoints his head and gives gifts to the Persians (claim)
events.note: HDT 9.110 (FT, Greek claim); the date is unknown, so it is not scheduled

events.name: the king sacrifices and gives gifts when he comes to Persia
events.note: Cyropaedia 8.5.21, 8.5.26 (FT, Greek claim; written of Cyrus, 'even to this day the great king ...')

events.name: birthday meal

goods.item: a small animal (sheep or goat) or better food

events.note: HDT 1.133: 'The day which every man values most is his own birthday' (FT, claim)

events.name: ploughing and sowing winter barley and wheat
preconditions: the first autumn rains have fallen (CE-20)
events.note: modern irrigated wheat: sown 2 Oct-10 Jan, normal 11 Nov-1 Dec (SX, B for modern Fars)

events.name: barley harvest
events.note: 'winter barley ... harvested between May and July' (SX, modern); IR-FOODAG harvest May-Jun; the plain's crop model cuts it by mid-June (plain.json). Window: days 33-66 = 15 May - 17 Jun in the seasons (20 May - 22 Jun Julian). Was months 1-3 (from 12 Apr), ahead of every source (Q-140)

events.name: wheat harvest
events.note: 'wheat harvest late May to late July'; rainfed mid-July (SX, modern); IR-FOODAG harvest Jun-Jul; the plain's crop model cuts it by mid-July (plain.json). Window: days 50-95 = 1 Jun - 16 Jul in the seasons (Q-140)

events.name: threshing, winnowing, grain to the stores
events.note: OP month 5 is 'harvest (month)' (SX); PF 6 delivery in months 4-6 (FT). Window: days 43-141 = 25 May - 31 Aug in the seasons, from ten days after the first reaping until the harvest month (Q-140)

events.name: spring sowing of summer crops (sesame attested)
events.note: PF 56 sesame (A); OP month 1 'sowing' gloss (SX, disputed)

events.name: vintage: grape harvest and pressing
effects: wine stock rises after 1-2 months -> E-09
events.note: no Fars source for the dates

events.name: fig and fruit harvest
events.note: figs are attested (PF 53); the season is C

events.name: shearing
effects: wool to households or the state (C)
events.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: Babylonian temple flocks were plucked or shorn in spring (Q-040)

events.name: lambing
events.note: no source

events.name: transhumant flocks pass through the plain

participants.role: herders: herding families (men, women, children, the old; lives.json herders, D-150)

events.note: modern Qashqai: north in April, south in September (SX, C analogue); no Achaemenid source. The Qashqai migrate as families, and HDT 1.125 (FT, a Greek claim) names four Persian tribes as all wandering herdsmen; a band is herding families, the make-up its analogue shows (D-150, lives.json herders)

events.name: canal and channel clearing
effects: irrigation capacity restored for the year
events.note: OP month 12 'digging-up' gloss (SX); canals and weirs are attested in the survey (SX)

events.name: river flow of the Pulvar and Kur
events.note: Pulvar today intermittent, often dry in summer and autumn (B); rain Nov-Apr (A)

events.name: daily building work (Hall of 100 Columns, Tripylon)
preconditions: not a rain day for outdoor tasks
events.note: gangs of ~100 + chief (SX, C)

events.name: construction progress

rule.unit: column shafts raised on the Hall of 100 Columns
rule.plus: wall courses and relief carving in proportion (C)

effects: geometry: +1 shaft about every 10 weeks of full-strength work
events.note: derived: ~70 shafts left in 467 (Q-012, ~30 % up) over ~15 years before completion under Artaxerxes I

events.name: winter slowdown: no mud-brick, mortar or plaster work on frost or rain days
effects: brick, mortar, plaster tasks suspended; stone dressing continues on dry days
events.note: frost 12-18 days/month and rain 5-6 days/month in Dec-Feb (A); the rule is C (Q-037)

events.name: mud-brick moulding and drying season
events.note: Babylonian month 3 is 'the month of the brick mould of the king' (Astrolabe B via extract; B for Babylonia, C for Persepolis)

events.name: midday rest in the heat
events.note: Tmax 36-38 C in Jun-Aug (A); the rule is C. Was months 3-5 only; the rest now follows the day's temperature, so a hot day in month 2 or 6 has it too and a cool day in month 4 does not (D-086)

events.name: rain: people shelter; outdoor work stops
events.note: rain days (>= 1 mm) 6.3/5.4/5.1 in Jan-Mar (A)

events.name: storm: all outdoor work stops; couriers still ride
events.note: thunder days 1.5-1.8 in Mar-Apr (A)

events.name: dust: travel and deliveries slow; faces covered
events.note: dust days peak Apr-Jul (A, x 0.5 per D-004)

events.name: birth

participants.role: women of her group or household (C)

effects: schedule(E-04) if in a ration group
events.note: Roman Egypt analogue (SX): female birth rate 'as high as 54 per thousand', argued too high; Q-039

events.name: death
events.place_kind: home -> burial ground outside the settlement (C)
effects: household shrinks; the person's ration stops (CE-16)
events.performance: the body is carried out of the settlement. Herodotus 1.140: Persians coat the body in wax and bury it; the magi first let birds or dogs tear it ('secretly and obscurely told'). Do not show exposure
events.note: e0 22-25 in Roman Egypt (SX) -> CDR ~40-45; infant mortality is RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN (Coale-Demeny West levels 2-4)

events.name: sickness episode
events.note: no source

events.name: marriage (household change only; no rite shown)
events.note: no rite attested for commoners at Persepolis, so no ceremony is performed

events.name: small dispute (ration shortfall, queue, tool, water turn)
effects: relationship between the two agents worsens (C)
events.note: no PF or PT dispute text retrieved

events.name: change of watch

participants.role: guards of the outgoing and incoming watch

events.note: reconstruction

events.name: Treasury guard doubled while silver is out or a courier is at the Treasury

rule.on: E-05 or E-20 at the Treasury

effects: guards at the Treasury x 2 for the duration
events.note: brief 9.1 (the Treasury is guarded when the king is away)

soak_variety_floor.basis: every week of the year, court absent, contains E-05, E-07, E-12, E-15, E-20, E-30, E-60, E-72, E-74, E-80 (10 kinds by id; 8 or more distinct 'kind' values) plus a seasonal farm or herd event; the first week of each month adds E-01/E-02/E-03
